methods.name: annotation_syntax_problem
methods.summary: Returns a description of the syntax problem if `x` is not valid annotation syntax, or `None` if valid. This only checks syntax; semantic validation (e.g. that `typing.Self` is in a class context) is handled elsewhere. See https://typing.re…

methods.name: body_contains_yield
methods.summary: Check if a body of statements syntactically contains `yield` or `yield from` at the current function scope level. Does not descend into nested function definitions, class definitions, or lambdas, since yields in those scopes belong to thos…

methods.name: decorator_trailing_name
methods.summary: The trailing identifier of a decorator expression, looking through calls and attribute access: `foo`, `mod.foo`, `foo(...)`, and `mod.foo(...)` all yield `foo`. `None` for shapes with no trailing name (e.g. a subscript).

methods.summary: Calls a function on all of the names bound by this lvalue expression.

methods.name: expr_name_identifier
methods.summary: We really want to avoid "making up" identifiers out of nowhere. But there, there isn't an identifier, but morally should be, so create the implicit one.

methods.name: flatten_dict_items
methods.summary: Pull all dictionary items up to the top level, so `{a: 1, **{b: 2}}` has the same items as `{a: 1, b: 2}`.

methods.name: has_docstring
methods.summary: Does the module have a docstring.

methods.name: if_branches
methods.summary: Iterates over the branches of an if statement, returning the test and body. A test on `None` is an `else` branch that is always taken.

methods.name: is_pytest_tracebackhide
methods.summary: Pytest reads `__tracebackhide__` from frame locals when formatting tracebacks, so an assignment to it is live even though no Python expression reads it.

methods.name: is_synthesized_empty_identifier
methods.summary: Same as `is_synthesized_empty_name` but for `Identifier` instead of `ExprName`.

methods.name: is_synthesized_empty_name
methods.summary: Returns true if this is a synthesized empty name from parser error recovery.

methods.name: needs_brackets
methods.summary: Whether `node` must be wrapped in parentheses to preserve its meaning when spliced in as a direct child of `parent` (the node that will contain it, or `None` when the containing node is unknown).

methods.summary: The tightest AST node that strictly contains `target` — i.e. the parent of the node whose range is `target`, or `None` at module top level.
